name: Amon
author: Paul Overy

provenance.from: AMOSTools/Extensions, out of aminet dev/amos/amostools.i386-aros.lha -- held in the corpus at sources/aminet-dev-amos/. Its author's README says the directory is "every AMOS extension I can find, cut down to just their token tables with the make_extensions.pl script", and names the ExoticA AMOS extensions wiki page as the list it works from.
provenance.redistribution: Not redistributed here as software: the file carries no code at all. It is a token table with the library stripped out from under it, kept for identification and detokenising.
provenance.note: ExoticA's AMOS extensions list places it at slot 15. Nothing here observes it in a program: the slot is the wiki's recommendation and no more.

notes: TABLE ONLY. This is an AMOSTools stub -- the hunk shell and the token table survive, both length fields read zero, there is no code, and every entry's two routine words are overwritten with `====`. So the NAMES, the parameter SPECS and, because an id is the byte offset of its entry, the IDS are the original library's; the behaviour is not here and the evidence tier cannot rise above `manual` until a real binary turns up. The reader is checked against CRAFT and MusiCRAFT, which are held both ways, and agrees with them entry for entry -- see parseAmosToolsTable in src/tokens/libtok.ts. 24 keywords and not one of them contested: a fast-maths and input block. `rodent *` is a mouse (`rodent x`, `set rodent`, `limit rodent`, `lrodent`, `rrodent`, `rodent key`), `fast angle`, `mul sin`, `mul cos`, `fast plot`, `fast point`, `fast circle` and `array plot` are the arithmetic, `keycode`/`key press` the keyboard, `joy3`/`joy4` two more sticks, and `count colour`/`find colour` search a screen. THE 1.03 AND 1.04 RELEASES ARE THE SAME FILE, byte for byte, so one entry covers both and 1.03 is vendored beside it as the proof.
